title: Microsoft Purview: DLP and auto-labeling policies for non-Microsoft connected apps
summary: Pass: the documented controls, licensing and usage meter are supported, and the briefing accurately distinguishes the preview documentation from the planned rollout. It also reports Microsoft's conflicting migration instructions rather than choosing between them. One checklist check lacks a matching control row.

claims.claim: The printed Purview DLP creation path follows the documented wizard through Enterprise applications & devices, Custom > Custom policy, Assign admin units > Full directory and Choose where to apply the policy.
claims.quote:
Go to Solutions > Data Loss Prevention > Policies > + Create policy.
On What info do you want to protect?, choose the Enterprise applications & devices option.
Select Custom > Custom policy, and then select Next.

claims.claim: No automation for the dedicated DLP application locations is documented on the researched feature and PowerShell reference pages.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview non-Microsoft connected apps dedicated locations New-DlpCompliancePolicy PowerShell API. Read the DLP feature page and New-DlpCompliancePolicy reference, including Locations and ThirdPartyAppDlpLocation; the latter links to the retiring Instances experience.

claims.claim: The printed auto-labeling path follows Solutions > Information protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > + Create auto-labeling policy, Automatically apply labels only, Custom > Custom policy and Choose a label to auto-apply > Choose a label.
claims.quote:
On What type of auto-labeling policy do you want to create?, choose Automatically apply labels only.
Select Custom > Custom policy > Next.
On Choose a label to auto-apply, choose Choose a label.

claims.claim: The auto-labeling wizard continues through Choose a sensitivity label > Add, Assign admin units > Full directory, and Choose locations where you want to apply the label.
claims.quote:
On Choose a sensitivity label, select all labels to include in the policy, and then select Add > Next.
On Assign admin units, the scope is set to Full directory.
On Choose locations where you want to apply the label

Go to Cloud Apps > Connected apps.

claims.claim: The retiring Instances path is Purview > Data loss prevention > Policies > + Create policy > Custom > Custom policy > Admin units > Locations > Instances > Edit > Specific instances > + Include instances.

On the Locations page, toggle the Instances location to on.
To select a specific app or instance, select Edit > Specific instances > + Include instances and then the instances (cloud apps) you want to include.

claims.quote: For more information about DLP for non-Microsoft cloud apps, see Use data loss prevention policies for non-Microsoft cloud apps.

claims.claim: The sources do not say the new dedicated policies change existing behaviour for tenants that create no policy.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview non-Microsoft connected applications DLP auto-labeling policies preview. Read the roadmap, supplied notice and both feature pages; new-policy configuration is described, not automatic enforcement. The briefing separately reports the existing file-policy retirement.

claims.claim: The roadmap and supplied notice do not describe a specific new end-user experience.

Each cloud app has its own enablement process based on the APIs it supports.
